C-SETTINGS-KEYBOARD-FOCUS.Name: Visible keyboard focus on shared Settings controls
C-SETTINGS-KEYBOARD-FOCUS.Summary: Give the existing switch, native select and segmented-control buttons a distinct keyboard-focus outline in both Settings and Quick Settings, using the established shared preference accent. The proposed treatment follows existing Quick Settings focus outlines; no palette or interaction redesign is proposed.
C-SETTINGS-KEYBOARD-FOCUS.Problem: DESIGN:F-002: real Chromium/WebKit keyboard probes in Paper and Ink reached focus-visible states on shared controls without any visible row/control change. Fourteen before/after screenshot comparisons were identical; four textbox positive controls changed. Selected/on styling cannot identify the current keyboard target.

Goals.R-1: For each enabled switch, native select and individual segment button, display a two-CSS-pixel outline in the existing prefAccent with a one-CSS-pixel offset when focus-visible is true, following the existing Quick Settings tab/open-all pattern.
Goals.R-2: Implement the presentation at the three existing shared component owners, so Settings and Quick Settings inherit the same treatment. Keep keyboard focus distinct from selected/on/nearest-preset state.
Goals.R-3: Preserve control and row geometry, labels, native selection menus, props/events, callbacks, saved preferences, disabled semantics, existing theme mapping and all consumers.

Constraints.Constraint: No JavaScript focus manager, tabindex changes, keyboard-policy changes, new events, IPC, preference keys, dependencies, OS settings, general global focus reset or parallel visual system.

Outline must remain visible without clipping in real Settings and Quick Settings at supported desktop sizes. If a required consumer cannot preserve geometry and focus visibility within the literal three-component scope, stop for a bounded scope revision.

Keep all existing failures, retries, skips, timeouts and coverage floors. Rendered evidence must use real keyboard input and identify any WebKit Option-Tab fallback; a synthetic focus() call alone is insufficient.
No implementation or plan until the proposed design/spec is explicitly approved. Do not mutate applied bundles or current graph/verification while this spec is draft.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Redesign Settings, repair narrow toolbar layout, alter tab order/radio navigation, modify textbox or slider styling, change system keyboard-access policy, supply owner/platform acceptance, or authorize a release.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Actual keyboard navigation yields a visible outline for all three enabled control types, including on/off switches and selected/unselected segments, in Paper and Ink. Disabled controls retain their current disabled and activation behavior.

Chromium and WebKit before/after captures visibly distinguish focus without changing row/control bounds, values or event counts. Tab away removes the additional outline; mouse-only activation does not force a keyboard indicator beyond browser focus-visible semantics.
Settings and Quick Settings consumers share the treatment without local copies. Existing selected/on/nearest-preset states and textbox positive controls remain intact.

A source-identified native macOS keyboard check verifies actual Settings/Quick Settings presentation when capture/input is available; otherwise the native item stays explicitly open. No owner/platform verdict is inferred from browser checks.

AffectedAreas.Verification: V-M-011; existing common-control tests plus a focused keyboard-presentation regression and real consumer evidence.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Focused real-keyboard Chromium/WebKit Paper/Ink captures, source/asset hashes, geometry/value/event invariants, Settings and Quick Settings consumer checks, retained textbox control and explicit native/owner boundaries. Exact commands and assertion files belong in the later approved execution plan.

GRACE current before editing; selected target/final assertions with commands; approved apply/archive and exact-head required hosted checks before integration, followed by Collecting train evidence without changing acceptance/release states.

Assumptions.Assumption: The existing Quick Settings focus-outline treatment is the proposed design authority. It is a recommendation, not a recorded owner choice. Approval adopts this short design and spec; execution-plan approval remains separate.
